facts.fact: UNDP states that with DHIS2 implemented the health ministry can now digitise and have immediately available aggregated health-care data at district level; it does not say whether facilities or district offices key the data.

UNDP states the digital tool was launched by the Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social, which leads the joint programme, and that the health database in the new Data Center at the ministry's Malabo headquarters is administered exclusively by the ministry.

UNDP states the DHIS2 implementation, the Data Center, training of more than 100 digital agents and donated equipment (50 laptops, 30 tablets, 20 desktops) came through the UN Joint Programme for strengthening the national health system (UNDP, WHO, UNICEF); no domestic budget is mentioned.

The health minister is quoted saying the digitalisation falls within the national health development plan PNDS 2021-2025, whose situation analysis names the lack of reliable health information sources as a priority problem; the plan is not said to name DHIS2.
The digital tool of the national health system, built on DHIS2, was officially launched at Baney on 1 March 2025 by the health ministry and UNDP.
